title: runtime: add memory-pressure guardrail to shed before KV-cache thrash/OOM + metrics
author: Samir Qureshi
description: Context: Under bursty long-context traffic we’ve seen a failure mode where GPU memory gets tight (KV cache fragmentation + allocator pressure). The scheduler continues admitting work, we start thrashing KV (high eviction/rehydrate), tail latency collapses, and we frequently end in OOM/driver reset. This PR adds a runtime-level memory-pressure guardrail that sheds deterministically *before* we enter the thrash/OOM spiral and emits standard metrics to support the Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding program. What’s in this PR: (1) MemoryPressureMonitor: samples device memory (free/total) and allocator pressure + KV cache signals (evictions/sec, pinned blocks) to derive a 3-state pressure level: normal / elevated / critical, with hysteresis + cooldown to avoid flapping. (2) Shed behavior: when pressure is elevated we stop admitting new requests at the runtime enqueue boundary once the bounded queue is above a low watermark; when pressure is critical we reject immediately at enqueue (no prefill scheduling) with an explicit reason code propagated upstream. For in-flight requests, we do *not* kill mid-token; we only shed before starting prefill for queued work. (3) KV-cache friendly backoff: on elevated pressure we temporarily reduce max concurrent prefill slots to give decode a chance to drain and free KV without ballooning. (4) Metrics + logs: adds counters and gauges to make this visible and to feed routing/gateway decisions later. Metrics are cardinality-safe (labels bounded to {gpu_pool, model_family} only; no tenant/request IDs). (5) Config knobs: thresholds and hysteresis can be tuned per GPU pool via config; defaults are conservative and gated behind a feature flag (runtime.mem_pressure_shed.enabled). Metrics introduced (names per observability review): runtime_mem_pressure_state{gpu_pool,model_family} (0/1/2), runtime_mem_pressure_transitions_total{from,to,gpu_pool,model_family}, runtime_shed_requests_total{reason="mem_pressure",shed_point="enqueue",gpu_pool,model_family}, runtime_kv_cache_evictions_total{gpu_pool,model_family}, runtime_kv_cache_eviction_rate{gpu_pool,model_family}. Testing: unit tests for the state machine + hysteresis; integration test that simulates a tight-memory environment using a fake allocator and forces critical state, asserting we shed at enqueue and do not deadlock the scheduler; perf-canary run on A10 pool with long prompts. Results: in the synthetic overload scenario (step traffic + long prompts), we saw 0 OOMs vs 3 OOMs in baseline, and p99 stabilized (still elevated, but no cliff). Notes: Upstream mapping to customer-facing 429/503 is not in this PR; this just ensures runtime fails fast with a deterministic reason instead of timing out/OOM. Related: ENG-4827; pairs with bounded queue shedding (ENG-4826) and overload reason propagation (PR-18494).
commits: runtime/memory-pressure: add MemoryPressureMonitor + state machine w/ hysteresis
runtime/scheduler: gate enqueue + prefill slot limits under elevated/critical pressure
runtime/metrics: add mem pressure + KV eviction metrics and structured log fields
runtime/config: add feature flag + pool-level threshold config
tests: unit + integration coverage for critical-pressure shed behavior
conversation: Noah Patel (review): Can you clarify why we don’t shed in-flight requests when pressure becomes critical? I’m worried we’ll still OOM if a bunch of requests are already in prefill. Samir Qureshi (author): Agreed concern. The monitor triggers based on allocator + KV signals that tend to show up *before* we’re at the cliff. In-flight prefill is the riskiest, but killing mid-prefill creates correctness issues and makes streaming behavior unpredictable. This PR only sheds at enqueue and before prefill scheduling; combined with the bounded queue cap, this should keep us from piling on additional prefill work. We can revisit “abort in prefill” as a separate ADR if needed. Omar El-Sayed (review): The KV eviction metric is useful. Can we include an eviction *rate* gauge so dashboards don’t require heavy PromQL? Also please make sure labels don’t include model name, only family/class. Samir: Added runtime_kv_cache_eviction_rate gauge computed in-process (EWMA over 10s) and restricted labels to model_family. Allison Grant (review): Metric label set looks OK but please avoid ‘from/to’ as free-form. Enumerate states and keep values bounded. Also make sure transition metric doesn’t explode cardinality. Samir: Transition metric uses from/to in {normal,elevated,critical} only. Added a comment and validation in registry init. Lena Fischer (review): Cooldown/hysteresis values: can we make them configurable per pool? The A100 pool recovers faster; A10 is slower. Samir: Added pool-level overrides in defaults.yaml + schema. Defaults: enter elevated at <12% free or eviction_rate>200/s; enter critical at <6% free or eviction_rate>400/s; cooldown 30s with 10s minimum stable period to close. Noah (follow-up): Please add a regression test for flapping (normal->elevated->normal within 5s) to ensure we don’t oscillate. Samir: Added unit test `TestMemoryPressure_HysteresisNoFlapOnTransientDip` and updated docs/internal/runtime/guardrails.md with the state diagram. Approved-by: Noah Patel, Omar El-Sayed, Lena Fischer, Allison Grant.
release_notes: Runtime now sheds deterministically on GPU memory pressure to prevent KV-cache thrash/OOM; emits new mem-pressure and KV eviction metrics for overload dashboards (feature-flagged: runtime.mem_pressure_shed.enabled).
